title: Start With the Constraint
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Dave Stuart Jr. tells how an offhand remark from the woman who became his wife reframed his first years of teaching. Her blunt reaction showed him that the goal of teaching is results for kids, not time spent or a savior-teacher self-image. From that point he adopted a fixed rule of stopping work at 5:30 pm and working backward from it. He explains the logic through Parkinson's Law: work that starts from the task list is endless, while work that starts from a constraint forces choices. Those choices push a teacher to ask what is most pointless and what the ultimate aim is. The essay is a teacher-workload and sustainability argument that ends on a crisp contrast between the average person and the teacher who can't afford to start with the work.
points: The point of teaching is the long-term flourishing of kids, not time spent or the image of the heroic, overworked teacher.
A hard stop (5:30 pm) turns an endless task list into a design problem: what can be done well in fifty hours a week.
Starting from the work lets it expand to fill all available time, per Parkinson's Law, while starting from the constraint forces prioritization.
Constraints surface better questions, such as what the most pointless task is and what the ultimate aim is, and open the door to satisficing and disciplined schedules.
quotes: Some days,” I told her, “the only time I see the sunlight is through the window of my classroom.” After saying this, I expected her to swoon at the noble warrior-poet who stood before her.

The objective of teaching isn’t to spend all your time doing it; the objective is to produce a certain set of results. She was pushing me along in my journey toward clarifying that the long-term flourishing of kids is what teaching is about, not the envisioning of oneself as the star of an imaginary, savior-style teacher movie.

Crystal helped me develop one of the most critical rules of my teaching career: I stop working at 5:30 pm. From this constraint, I’ve worked backward: How do I get done what needs to be done between 7:30 am and 5:30 pm on weekdays?
When we start with the work that needs to be done, the work is endless and it is impossible to complete. It fills whatever space we'll give it; this is called Parkinson’s Law.

But when we start with the constraints, we have to work from those. Suddenly we can’t do every possible thing — and so we have to ask questions like “What is the most pointless thing I do?” and “What am I ultimately aiming for?
The average person starts with the work. You and I can’t afford to do that. So we start with the constraint.
